findings.defect: Every daylight view with a large plume is rendered about 2.5 to 3 stops under-exposed. Measured sRGB: sky (31,42,62) and sunlit ground (60,52,41) in the pad and booster scenes, against sky (88,103,127) and ground (125,115,101) in the same lab scene with a small engine at minimum throttle. A noon lift-off reads as dusk with a navy sky. Because the meter holds the flame under white, the 1e6 cd/m2 core barely clips (0 pixels at or above 250 in engine-atlas-9m/sl-full.png, 28 in liftoff/t10-day.png) and has no bloom, so the jets look pastel. The same mechanism makes the frame pump: in the splash sequence the sky goes 208 -> 88 and the sea green channel 123 -> 18 between 'before' and '+1 s' while the crown itself is rendered grey (max 200); in the explosion sequence the sky goes 70 -> 111 over 3.5 s.
findings.realReference: Daylight launch footage (Saturn V, Falcon 9, SLS): sky, pad and terrain stay at normal daylight exposure; the flame is a clipped white-yellow core with glare around it and the steam cloud is brilliant white. A splash crown or a fireball does not darken the ocean or the sky around it.
findings.likelyCause: The exposure meter, not the plume data. src/render/core/post/exposureMeter.ts (lines 23-29) builds its histogram from the final HDR target at every pixel that has geometry depth, i.e. after the vfx transparents are composited. src/render/core/post/exposure.ts line 203 then raises EV until the histogram's p99 is below HIGHLIGHT_CAP (4 x mid grey), at full weight from a 2 % lit fraction (LIT_FULL_BRIGHT). A plume, plume-lit steam or a white crown in front of geometry therefore sets the exposure. The cap in src/render/vfx/feature.ts (DAYLIGHT_WHITE = 12000, lines 141 and 175) only limits the hint for emitters over sky and does not touch this path, so hand-off section 5.12 ('by day a plume leaves the exposure where the sun puts it and clips') does not hold in the pictures.
findings.fixDirection: File a request to core-support: meter the HDR target before drawTransparent (or accept an exclusion for emissive transparents), and bound highlight protection to the sunny-16 prior plus about 0.5 EV while the sun is up so that flames clip by 2 to 3 stops and bloom. Then re-shoot the lift-off, ascent, splash and explosion sheets, and add a spec that the sky luminance of the pad scene changes by less than 0.5 EV between engines off and engines on by day.

findings.defect: From the front the shock layer is a pinwheel: streaks radiate from one pole at the stagnation point (a visible pinch), inside a hard-edged inner ellipse, surrounded by a ring of crystalline 'glitter' cells, with a dark notch where the shoulder cuts the ring. From behind it is a flat mauve disc inside a white glitter ring (a solar-eclipse look), hairline orange sparks in one quadrant only, and a soft mauve veil over the left third of the frame. Close up the glitter is a lattice of about 2 px cells along the heat-shield rim.
findings.realReference: Orion EFT-1 / Artemis I and Apollo onboard footage: a smooth, flickering sheath of orange-pink to white gas streaming past the shoulder, no fixed pattern on the shield face, streamers shed irregularly, ablation sparks all round. From outside (airborne observation of Hayabusa, Stardust, ATV-1): a compact white-orange head with a soft glow, no ring and no spokes.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vfx/plasma.ts lines 269-288: the streak noise is stretched along v = x - n * n.x, which vanishes at the stagnation point (clamped at 0.05), so every streak converges on a pole. plasmaBody (lines 195-209) switches between the spherical cap and the rim, which changes the wall normal abruptly: that is the hard inner ellipse. Beyond the shoulder the noise lod (t * fp * 1.5 / Rb) is far below a half-resolution pixel and aliases into the cell pattern. The veil is what remains of the wake after the near-eye cut (hand-off section 6).
findings.fixDirection: Blend from isotropic, time-varying turbulence at the stagnation point to streaks only where |v| is large; use a rounded body distance so the normal is continuous across cap and shoulder and let thickness and brightness vary smoothly there. Band-limit the shoulder noise to the pixel footprint and end the layer with a soft falloff rather than a ring. Emit sparks all round the rim. Fade the wake symmetrically around the eye so no one-sided veil is left.

findings.defect: At +0.1 s the splash is a flat white ellipse with a fur of straight radial needles. At +0.4 s the crown is a smooth-walled truncated cone (a lampshade) of uniform light grey with a few sawtooth notches on its rim; it reads as a solid mesh. At +1 s it is blurred low-resolution blobs with blotchy holes through which the capsule shows, plus round soft 'mist ball' discs beside it. Droplets are uniform small grey dashes of one size, evenly spread in an annulus and darker than the crown. The foam is a perfect ellipse with a hard outer edge, a lace-like speckle inside and single dark-blue pinhole pixels.
findings.realReference: Apollo, Orion and Dragon splashdown footage: an irregular bright white wall of water thrown up and outward asymmetrically (the capsule arrives with horizontal speed), breaking at once into ragged curtains and chunky spray of very different sizes, a central rebound, then an irregular foam patch with streaky edges over pale turquoise aerated water.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vfx/splash.ts: the crown is an axisymmetric thin sheet about the vertical with analytic rise and lean, marched at half resolution (crown.steps 30) and lit almost uniformly (lines 188-189: sun x 0.38..0.8 plus ambient), so its wall has no shading; tearing acts only near the rim (line 181). The foam radius is one analytic circle (line 312) with a smoothstep edge (line 89). Droplets are particles clamped to one pixel of radius (src/render/vfx/particles.ts lines 344-350) with their own, dimmer lighting.
findings.fixDirection: Break the symmetry: per-azimuth launch speed, height and tear time from low-frequency noise, biased by the entry velocity. Give the sheet thickness variation, forward-scatter and self-shadow so it reads as water, and hand its upper half to particles of widely varying size earlier. Light droplets with the crown's radiometry. Perturb the foam outline with two or three noise octaves and drift streaks, tint the water under it, and filter the threshold so no pinholes remain.

findings.defect: Thin dark wavy lines (about 2 px at 1440p, 1 px at 720p) run through the bright cloud on both sides of the jet, from where the jet enters the cloud down towards the pad, like cracks in the smoke. They are present with live temporal filtering, so they are not a property of the deterministic screenshots.
findings.realReference: A steam and exhaust cloud is continuous around the flame; nothing outlines the flame inside it.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vfx/smoke.ts: each quarter-resolution ray splits its smoke into 'in front of' and 'behind' the emitters at tE, and tE exists only where the summed moment weight exceeds 1e-4 (lines 292-293), otherwise it is infinite. The combine pass (lines 496-524) interpolates the front and back results separately between four rays. Across the contour of the plume image's faint edge neighbouring rays use different splits (all smoke in front versus front plus back), and F.rgb + F.a * B.rgb of the interpolated values comes out darker than either ray. The contour follows the plume's ragged halo, hence wavy lines beside the jet.
findings.fixDirection: Make the split continuous across rays: dilate tE over the 3 x 3 quarter-resolution neighbourhood, or split at the plume cluster's analytic distance inside its screen rectangle. Alternatively compose each tap with the pixel's own emitter value first and interpolate the composed results. Add a spec: a plume image faded to zero must give the same picture as no plume.

findings.defect: Pad smoke: (a) near-black holes inside the sunlit cloud with ragged, dendritic or stair-stepped edges (about 4 px blocks at 720p), still there with live filtering; (b) the thin fringe of the cloud breaks into a blocky checker of light and dark squares instead of fading out; (c) round peach discs of similar size sit in rows inside the cloud near the jet; (d) the body of the cloud is rounded cells of one size and is soft everywhere, so sharp holes sit inside a blurred mass.
findings.realReference: Launch clouds are optically thick: gaps show darker self-shadowed cloud, never black ground; edges are wispy curls over a continuous range of scales; the glow near the flame is a smooth flickering gradient.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vfx/smoke.ts lines 392-394: erosion multiplies the density by saturate((billow - erosion * (1 - cover)) * 4 + cover), a steep threshold that cuts patches to zero; behind them the ground has been darkened by the cloud-shadow multiply (SHADOW_WGSL, padSmoke.groundShadow 0.85), so the holes are nearly black. The quarter-resolution march with per-pixel jitter and the depth-weighted bilinear combine cannot resolve the eroded fringe (4 px blocks). Lines 413-414: glow = heat to the 16th power of a trilinearly filtered grid channel, which turns each hot cell into an isolated round blob. Billows come from two noise octaves on one base scale (erosionScale 0.016 and 3.1 x).
findings.fixDirection: Erode with a soft remap that keeps a density floor away from the rim, and add a multiple-scattering ambient term so gaps read as grey cloud. Resolve the fringe at half resolution or filter the quarter-resolution result before the combine. Replace heat^16 with a smooth emission curve evaluated after the noise displacement (or blur the heat channel). Add at least two more detail octaves with a wider range of scales.

findings.view: C:/dev/fable-space-game/out/screens/vfx/liftoff/t0-night.png, liftoff/t3-night.png, liftoff/t10-night.png, liftoff-chase/t0-night.png, liftoff-chase/t6-night.png, explosion/night-0.2s.png, explosion/night-1.5s.png
findings.defect: At night the nine-engine plume lights the launch mount (clipped white) and the smoke, but the pad surface, the surrounding ground and the vehicle body stay at 0 to 4 of 255, even with a 6 x gain applied to the picture. The night fireball likewise lights nothing beneath it and has no glow halo. The brief asks for ground and smoke lit by the plume.
findings.realReference: Night launches light the pad, the tower and kilometres of landscape orange-white, and the vehicle's aft glows; an explosion at night lights the ground and its own smoke.
findings.likelyCause: Three things add up. (1) The exposure (first finding): the brightest plume-lit steam sets it and the ground sits about 9 stops lower. (2) src/render/vfx/feature.ts lines 213-221: one capsule light per cluster from the nozzle exit to 1.2 x core length along the jet; from T+0 to about T+3 that segment ends below the pad plane, so for ground points the nearest point of the light is at or under the surface and N.L is near zero, while the hull above the nozzles sees it end-on. (3) Data: light.efficacy 8.5 cd/N gives about 6e7 cd for the booster, roughly ten times less than what lights a pad like daylight; explosion.luminance 70,000 and lightEfficacy 0.008 are low.
findings.fixDirection: End the capsule at the plume foot and add a second light at the impingement point for the spreading flame and the lit steam; raise the efficacy (aim for about 1e4 lux at 300 m from the booster). Make the fireball a sphere light of its own radius. Add a spec that the pad 50 to 150 m from the mount exceeds a luminance threshold at night with engines on.

findings.view: C:/dev/fable-space-game/out/screens/vfx/engine-atlas-9m/30km-full.png, engine-atlas-9m/60km-full.png, engine-atlas-9m/vac-full.png, engine-atlas-9m/vac-min.png, engine-vela-2/vac-full.png, engine-vela-2v/vac-full.png, engine-lyra-d/vac-full.png, engine-lyra-a/vac-full.png, plumes-close/vacuum-60m.png, vacuum-ignition/ignition-4s.png, ascent/60km.png
findings.defect: From 60 km up every engine's plume is a small closed teardrop with a rounded outline (about 80 px for vela, 40 px for lyra at 720p), filled with a repeating pattern of elongated light blobs (leopard spots). At 30 km the fan shows the same cells in rows. The six-engine upper stage is a small blue speckled puff. The brief's progression ends in 'vast and faint'; these are compact and textured.
findings.realReference: In near vacuum the exhaust turns almost 90 degrees from the axis and has no outer boundary: a huge, smooth, very faint umbrella whose brightness falls with distance squared (best seen sunlit, as in the twilight 'jellyfish' of a Falcon 9 second stage), with a small bright region at the nozzle exit and no texture.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vfx/plumes.ts: emission is confined to rBulk = min(rb, 2 re + BULK_SLOPE x) (line 123) and decays as exp(-x / cells.z) over core.vacuumLengthRe of 6 to 11 exit radii (data/defs/visuals/plumes.json), then is closed by the window at 0.8 to 1.0 of the box length (lines 180-181); the halo that reaches the true boundary carries only smoke.halo 0.2 of the particulates. The cells are the streak-noise octaves (lines 311-334, noise.amount 0.4 to 0.55) at full strength where the gas should be smooth.
findings.fixDirection: Beyond the shock-cell window switch to a far-field model: density proportional to cos^n(theta * pi / (2 thetaMax)) / r^2 from the nozzle with no closed boundary, self-emission near the exit and sunlight scattering beyond, bounds of hundreds of exit radii with steps scaled by screen coverage. Fade the turbulence noise to zero as ambient pressure falls.

findings.defect: The ignition flash is a flat cream ellipse standing across the engine axis, with a sharp downstream face and a speckled edge: it reads as a lens or halo sprite stuck on the stage. The ullage motors are two cream blobs beside the interstage with no jets. The planet behind darkens for the flash frames (exposure pump).
findings.realReference: Upper-stage ignition in vacuum (J-2, Merlin Vacuum, RL10 footage): a brief, wide, translucent puff of unburnt propellant that expands in all directions and washes over the stage below, then a faint steady plume; ullage motors are short bright conical jets with thin smoke.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vfx/plumes.ts line 159: the flash is a Gaussian ball exp(-(r / (1.3 rBulk + re))^2) * exp(-x / 8 re), multiplied by the start-up 'front' (line 114) which cuts it at the distance the front has run. In the first tenths of a second that is a few metres, so the ball is sliced into a thin slab seen as a disc. Flash colour and luminance are uniform.
findings.fixDirection: Model the flash as an expanding shell of gas that fills forward and sideways (radius grows with frontSpeed x age in every direction away from the nozzle, soft on all sides), with density noise and a fade, instead of a ball cut by a plane. In vacuum let it spread widely and thin out; give ullage and retro motors a visible core jet.

findings.defect: Solid-motor plumes in air are flat beige wedges with ruler-straight edges and pencil-point tips, uniformly stippled, with no incandescent core and no billowing; four of them read as paper cones or searchlight beams. Above 30 km they become a faint bulb with a bright parabolic outline. (The hand-off lists this as a weakness; it is included because a player sees it at a glance during an abort.)
findings.realReference: Abort-motor and booster tests (Orion PA-1 and AA-2, SRB firings): a blinding white-yellow flame for several nozzle diameters, then dense white-grey smoke with a turbulent, cauliflower edge that widens irregularly and is lit and shadowed by the sun.
findings.likelyCause: data/defs/visuals/plumes.json plume.solid: smoke.extinction 1.6 with sunScatter 1.2 makes the jet opaque from the lip, so the 1.5e6 cd/m2 core is buried; the boundary is the analytic cone of src/render/vfx/plumes.ts jetGeom (lines 79-92) with maxExpansionDeg 30, and the 'ragged' edge (line 164) displaces it by a few per cent only. The smoke is lit by one unshadowed sun term (line 316), hence the flat colour.
findings.fixDirection: Delay the particulates (optically thin for the first 5 to 10 exit radii so the flame shows), then grow billows with large-amplitude, multi-octave displacement of the boundary that increases downstream, and add self-shadowing along the sun direction (two or three shadow steps or an analytic depth term). Consider handing the far smoke to the trail system with real turbulence.

findings.defect: Separation is a lumpy cream glow around the interstage; where it crosses the hull edge the edge is eaten in rounded scallops. Retro motors are a diffuse blob with two clumps of identical small square-ish white dots and scattered orange squares (pixel confetti): no jets, no streaks, no size variation. At coast the gap is surrounded by beige dots of one size.
findings.realReference: Staging footage (Saturn V, Falcon 9, Titan): short, sharply defined bright jets from each retro motor with thin smoke, a brief flash, a few tumbling pieces of very different sizes, and a thin expanding translucent gas ring; the stages' edges stay crisp.
findings.likelyCause: Retro and ullage motors use plume.solid at vacuum pressure, where the core is hidden as in the previous finding. The scallops come from compositing the half-resolution volume over a hull edge with the core's depth-aware upsample (src/render/vfx/volumes.ts lines 45-54): the half-resolution depth alternates between hull and background along the edge. The dots are particles clamped to a radius of one pixel (src/render/vfx/particles.ts lines 344-350), so every sub-pixel particle becomes the same 2 px dot.
findings.fixDirection: Give each motor a visible core jet (see solids). In the composite, reject the volume where its mean distance (the moment target) lies behind the full-resolution depth, so a near edge is never brightened by a far volume. For particles, keep the energy-conserving widening but vary size and brightness per particle, stretch fast ones by exposure time, and reduce the count in favour of a few larger pieces.

findings.view: C:/dev/fable-space-game/out/screens/vfx/reentry/plasma-1.0-day.png, reentry/plasma-0.3-day.png, reentry/plasma-1.0-night.png, reentry/trail-50km-day.png, reentry/trail-50km-night.png, haze-trail-50km.png, dev/f9-int-reentry-side.png
findings.defect: Chase view: the shock cap is a clipped white lens with a crisp rim and no colour gradient; the wake is a uniform dusty-mauve tube of straight streaks, the same hue from head to tail. From 50 km the trail is a ruler-straight bar of constant width and constant brightness across the whole frame, ending in a hard square cap with a gap of a few pixels before a tiny yellow dot (the vessel): a drawn line with no bright head. The ascent trail in haze-trail-50km.png has the same constant width and hard ends.
findings.realReference: Reentry from outside: the head is the brightest thing in the frame (white-orange, with glare), the luminous tail fades within a second or two behind it and narrows, then a faint persistent train; colour runs from white at the head through orange to dull red. Ascent trails widen with age and are kinked by wind shear.
findings.likelyCause: data/defs/visuals/plumes.json reentry.trail: lifetime 18 s (135 km of glow at 7.5 km/s) and luminance 26,000 keep the whole trail above display white. src/render/vfx/trail.ts lines 117-119 and 186-188 widen every sub-pixel tube to one pixel, which gives the constant width; the fade-in at the newest end spans only the wake volume (lines 335-342), which is sub-pixel at 50 km, hence the square cap and the gap. The plasma volume itself is sub-pixel at that range and is not widened or handed to bloom, so there is no head. Wake colour is one value from reentry.colors for the whole volume.
findings.fixDirection: Shorten the glow to 1 to 2 s with a faint long-lived train, grade colour and width with age, and draw the head as an energy-conserving point (widened to a pixel, at its full integrated intensity) so it clips and blooms; join trail and head without a gap. In the chase view grade the cap from white at the stagnation region to orange-pink at the shoulder and let the wake cool in colour along its length.

findings.view: C:/dev/fable-space-game/out/screens/vfx/explosion/day-0.03s.png, explosion/day-0.2s.png, explosion/day-0.6s.png, explosion/day-1.5s.png, explosion/day-3.5s.png, explosion/day-7s.png, explosion/close-0.6s.png, explosion/close-2.5s.png, explosion/night-0.2s.png
findings.defect: The fireball never clips: no pixel reaches 250 in all channels in any day or night frame, and the first frame (0.03 s) is a dim pale-orange ball. Fragment trails are pale salmon rods of constant width with rounded ends and a visible joint near the tip (a sea-urchin look). Secondary fireballs are crunchy high-frequency balls, one with a nearly square outline, beside a main ball that is blurred as if out of focus. The smoke is a soft tan blob with no dark soot. Debris appears as vertical columns of evenly spaced dots (about 3 px period) and cool white specks. A short dark vertical bar crosses the left trail in close-2.5s.png.
findings.realReference: Vehicle explosions (Antares Orb-3, AMOS-6, N1): the first frames are a clipped white flash that lights everything, then turbulent orange-yellow fire with black soot mixed in from the start, sharp cauliflower detail at all scales, burning fragments on arcs with thick dark-and-bright turbulent trails, and debris of every size.
findings.likelyCause: data/defs/visuals/plumes.json explosion.luminance 70,000 cd/m2 is only about twice a sunlit white surface, and the meter then holds it under white (first finding). src/render/vfx/fireball.ts marches 40 steps at half resolution with three low-frequency noise octaves for the main ball, while the secondaries use the same noise on a much smaller radius (hence sharper) and their bound clips them. Fragment trails are trail.ts tubes with noise amount cut for glowing nodes (line 434) and widened to a pixel. The dot columns are chips emitted from one point with the same velocity on successive steps (director.ts around line 534-559).
findings.fixDirection: Raise the peak luminance by about an order of magnitude with a white flash in the first 50 ms, mix dark soot into the fire from the start (absorbing lobes), add finer detail octaves to the main ball and scale noise frequency with radius so secondaries match. Give fragment trails turbulence, width growth and a bright head. Randomise chip spawn position, time and velocity within the step.

findings.view: C:/dev/fable-space-game/out/screens/vfx/lunar/30m-day.png, lunar/10m-day.png, lunar/5m-day-close.png, lunar/3m-night.png, lunar/30m-night.png, perf-lunar-descent-with-dust.png, dev/f9-int-lunar-surface.png
findings.defect: The dust sheet is a flat starburst of straight radial rays painted on the ground, with no height or parallax and a darker oval directly under the lander regardless of the sun direction (the lander's real shadow is far to the right). In the deterministic 720p shots it is also a stipple of 2 to 4 px speckles; the live 1440p perf shot shows the stipple resolves, the rays and short dashes remain. At 3 m by night it is a radial field of white dots and dashes around a clipped blob (a warp-starfield look). The lander's own plume at night is a bright lampshade cone with a hard flat top at the nozzle, not 'nearly invisible with a faint core'; a strut crossing it is drawn as a dotted line.
findings.realReference: Apollo descent film (16 mm DAC): a thin, fast, ground-hugging sheet streaming radially, smooth and bright in forward scatter, that blurs and hides the surface and the horizon below about 10 m; streaks are fine, continuous and flicker; rocks cast long shadows across it. The descent engine plume is essentially invisible.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vfx/dust.ts: 10 stretches per ray (particles.dust.sheetSteps) with one jittered sample each (lines 99-103); streaks are two noise lookups in angle (lines 117-119) with little radial variation, so they are straight spokes; the sheet's height scale is small and the in-scatter is weak against the lab's bright ground, so dense dust near the foot only darkens it (lines 120-126). Dust particles are one-pixel streaks (particles.ts). The plume: plume.methalox-lander core.vacuumGain 0.045 and vacuumCoreRe 3 leave a bright near field at the night exposure. The dotted strut is sub-pixel geometry in a frame without temporal jitter, possibly helped by the half-resolution composite.
findings.fixDirection: Make the sheet volumetric in appearance: more stretches near the foot, streak noise that varies and breaks along the radius and scrolls outward, stronger forward scattering towards low sun, and enough optical depth below 10 m to veil the ground and horizon. Remove the dark core by balancing extinction against in-scatter. Lower the lander's vacuum near-field brightness. Check the strut with live jitter before changing anything there.

findings.view: C:/dev/fable-space-game/out/screens/vfx/chutes/mains-reef1-backlit.png, chutes/mains-reef2-backlit.png, chutes/mains-full-backlit.png, chutes/mains-full-frontlit.png, chutes/drogues-reefed.png, splash/cut-away-6s.png, perf-chutes-and-splash.png
findings.defect: Canopies pass through each other at every stage: two reefed mains merge, at the second stage three spheres intersect, and at full inflation the lower canopy's crown pokes into the upper one's skirt. Reefed mains are smooth brick-patterned ellipsoids with a ragged polygonal hem. The suspension lines stay light grey when the capsule is a black silhouette against the light. At distance the gore and ring pattern aliases into single saturated orange, white and blue pixels. One second after cut-away the canopies still hover as full domes over taut straight cones of lines that end in mid-air.
findings.realReference: Orion and Apollo recovery footage: clustered canopies press against each other and deform, never overlap; a reefed ring-sail is a narrow wrinkled tube with an inflated crown; lines against the sun are dark; after cut-away the lines go slack at once and the canopy deflates and crumples within a second or two, then settles as a sheet.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vfx/canopyModel.ts clusterAngle (lines 210-215) spaces the canopies by the projected skirt radius at the current inflation, while the drawn bulb is wider than its skirt when reefed and breathing and flutter add to it; nothing resolves contact. src/render/vfx/chutes.ts line 207 lights lines as 'half faces the sun whatever the view'. The pattern is evaluated per fragment without filtering (lines 127-133). Cut-away: inflation falls as exp(-age / 3.5 s) (line 544-545) and all lines run straight to one confluence point (lines 559-563).
findings.fixDirection: Space by the maximum radius of the generated profile plus flutter amplitude and add a contact pass that pushes or flattens canopies where they would overlap. Make line brightness depend on the angle between view and sun. Filter the pattern by screen-space derivatives. On cut-away release line tension at once (catenary sag per line, no common point) and collapse the canopy within 1 to 1.5 s with asymmetric folding.

findings.defect: Sunlit RCS firings are long, collimated, uniformly grey beams with straight edges and soft ends, like torch beams in fog, several metres long at constant density. In shadow the frame is nearly black; with gain the centre thruster's glow shows a horizontal step where it meets the hull edge and blocky half-resolution stair-steps along the hull silhouette.
findings.realReference: Shuttle, Dragon and Apollo thruster firings in vacuum: a brief bright flash at the nozzle and a wide, quickly thinning translucent cone (tens of degrees half-angle) that is gone within a metre or two; pulses are sharp in time.
findings.likelyCause: data/defs/visuals/plumes.json plume.rcs: maxExpansionDeg 10, smoke.halo 0.9, smoke.lengthRe 70 and sunScatter 14 make a filled narrow cone that scatters sunlight evenly along 70 exit radii. The step and stair-steps come from the half-resolution volume against the hull edge in the core's depth-aware upsample (src/render/vfx/volumes.ts lines 45-54).
findings.fixDirection: Widen the cone to 30 to 45 degrees with density falling as 1 / r^2 from the nozzle, shorten the visible length, keep a small bright root, and make the pulse envelope sharp. For the hull edge, reject volume samples whose mean distance is behind the full-resolution depth, or draw RCS puffs at full resolution (they are small on screen).

findings.view: C:/dev/fable-space-game/out/screens/vfx/plumes-close/booster-45m.png, reentry-views/side-close-1.0.png, reentry/plasma-0.3-day.png, lunar/5m-day-close.png, engine-atlas-9m/10km-full.png (compare dev/f8-booster-45m-live.png and perf-lunar-descent-with-dust.png, which are smooth)
findings.defect: With no temporal history the half-resolution volumes show their per-pixel jitter as a 2 px diamond lattice or speckle over plumes, plasma and dust. The matrix is shot in deterministic mode, so all of its close-ups carry it; live shots are smooth. A player will see the same lattice for a few frames after every camera cut, on disocclusion and under fast camera motion.
findings.realReference: Gas and dust are smooth at pixel scale in every frame.
findings.likelyCause: One blue-noise offset per half-resolution pixel on a 10 to 30 step march (src/render/vfx/plumes.ts line 295, plasma.ts line 248, dust.ts line 86, smoke.ts line 342), with the result relying on the core's temporal filter; the upsample in src/render/vfx/volumes.ts does no spatial filtering of its own.
findings.fixDirection: Add a small depth-aware spatial filter (3 x 3 or a-trous) on the half-resolution volume image before the composite, or keep a vfx-owned history for the volume targets. Also shoot one live frame per matrix sheet so reviews see what a player sees.

findings.defect: At chase distance the nine jets are a curtain of parallel vertical stripes with rows of soft white blobs (shock cells as blurred beads, not diamonds). In ascent/12km.png one isolated white comma-shaped blob floats inside the merged plume.
findings.realReference: Clustered methalox or kerolox engines at lift-off: individual jets with crisp, bright Mach diamonds in the first few diameters that merge into one turbulent flame with large-scale flicker; no lone bright spot downstream.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vfx/plumes.ts: shock cells are Gaussian discs (lines 130-136) and streak noise is laid on at the mean emission depth (lines 326-334), which the hand-off names as a texture. The lone blob is probably one nozzle's late shock cell surviving in the blend zone between the separate jets and the merged jet (weights 1 - w, lines 184-201); not confirmed.
findings.fixDirection: Sharpen the cells into the oblique-shock diamond shape with a bright disc, limited to the first cells per nozzle, and drive the merged region with large-scale turbulence instead of per-jet streaks. Fade each nozzle's cell term to zero before the blend to the merged jet begins.

findings.defect: With the camera inside the pad cloud the whole frame is one flat orange-tan fill with the mount as a faint silhouette and a hard-edged darker wedge on the ground: no gradient towards the jet, no structure.
findings.realReference: Inside a plume-lit cloud the light falls off steeply away from the flame and the fog shows moving gradients and darker pockets.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vfx/smoke.ts: the march ends once transmittance is below 0.003 (line 443), a few metres in a dense cloud, where the plume term and the heat glow are nearly constant; the wedge is the screen-space ground-shadow multiply showing through.
findings.fixDirection: Add the direction-dependent plume term (brighter towards the jet) for near samples and keep large-scale density variation close to the eye; fade the ground-shadow multiply when the eye is inside the cloud.

findings.defect: The canopies' shadows on the water have a stippled upper edge and fine horizontal stripes inside (moire) at the grazing view.
findings.realReference: A soft-edged, even shadow that follows the swell.
findings.likelyCause: Probably the core's shadow filter on the lab's flat ocean in a frame without temporal jitter (the canopies are drawn in the everyFrame cascades by src/render/vfx/chutes.ts); the stripes look like depth-bias moire at a grazing sun. Not confirmed in vfx code.
findings.fixDirection: Check on the real ocean with live filtering; if it persists, raise the slope-scaled bias for the canopy caster or report to core-support with this picture.
